objectives.summary: The ThaBIT project aims to develop a versatile 3D environment that enhances user interaction with computers. Key objectives include completing the Alpha version by late April, releasing a beta version by mid-summer, and providing an open-source platform for users to create and share plugins.
key_points: The project aims to finish the current stage by late April and push the Alpha version to friends and contributors.
The beta version of ThaBIT could be expected by the end of summer, possibly mid-summer.
ThaBIT aims to provide an environment for users to create and share their own plugins.
The primary goals of ThaBIT include Internet Browsing, File System Browsing, and interaction with network devices.
The project is focused on the open-source community and aims to inspire others to create similar software packages.
ThaBIT is a versatile 3D environment written in C++ that primarily serves as a user interface wrapper.

strategy.summary: The ThaBIT project aims to create a versatile 3D environment that enhances user interaction through a natural interface. The strategy includes developing networking features, supporting user-generated plugins, and obtaining photorealistic 3D models. The team plans to utilize Kickstarter funding to cover essential expenses and has set a lower funding goal to improve chances of success.

The project aims to allow users to create and share their own plugins.
The team plans to finish the base framework before releasing Alpha 1 and polishing in Beta 1.
ThaBIT is working on networking features, including file sharing and P2P networking.

innovation.summary: ThaBIT introduces innovative features such as configurable 'Worlds' that can represent various local environments or network devices. The platform supports the creation of plugins, including a Browser and Video Player, and allows for the integration of 3D objects, enhancing user interaction with a versatile 3D environment.
key_points: ThaBIT organizes environments in configurable units called 'Worlds'.
Each World can represent multiple local environments or network devices.
Plugins for ThaBIT can be easily created, with documentation and source code provided.
Supported plugins include a Browser, Picture viewer, Video Player, and File manager.
3D Objects in ThaBIT can be any 3D Studio Max object or a group of objects.

feasibility.summary: The ThaBIT project is currently 60% complete, with 80% of the backend finished and 40% of the front end remaining. The project is based in Toronto, Canada, and aims to finish the current stage by late April, with a beta version expected by the end of summer. The project has received $411 in funding and is driven by a Kickstarter campaign that emphasizes community support to expedite completion.
